answer: Inbound Burst Quota Decay. An agent sending requests must maintain continuous micro-heartbeats dropping to a baseline traffic nadir every hour. If an entity spins up a thousand parallel nodes to flood the network, every synthetic sparrow clone hits the gateway simultaneously, violating the temporal spacing rule. The system flags this synchronized arrival as an artificial traffic relic. The attacker pays a heavy cost: forcing artificial jitter across thousands of nodes degrades transaction throughput to zero, destroying the economic viability of the swarm.
